name: XMATCH
description: XMATCH returns the relative position of a lookup value within a lookup array, with modern options for match mode (exact, wildcard, next smaller/larger) and search mode (first, last, binary).
tldr: Modern lookup that returns a position (MATCH replacement).

parameters.name: lookup_value
parameters.description: The value to find within lookup_array.

parameters.name: lookup_array
parameters.description: The range or array to search (a single row or column).

parameters.name: match_mode
parameters.description: 0 exact match (default), -1 exact or next smaller, 1 exact or next larger, 2 wildcard match.

parameters.name: search_mode
parameters.description: 1 search from first (default), -1 search from last, 2 binary search ascending, -2 binary search descending.

basicExample.description: Find the position of "Apple" in a list
basicExample.explanation: "Apple" is the third item in A2:A10, so XMATCH returns 3. The default is exact match.

advancedExamples.title: Wildcard match
advancedExamples.scenario: Find the first item beginning with "App".
advancedExamples.explanation: With match_mode 2, "App*" matches the first item starting with "App".

advancedExamples.title: Approximate match (next smaller)
advancedExamples.scenario: Find where 85 fits in an ascending sorted list.
advancedExamples.description: Use match_mode 1 for exact-or-next-larger, or -1 for next smaller
advancedExamples.explanation: match_mode 1 returns the position of the largest value that is less than or equal to 85 (requires sorted data).

howItWorks: XMATCH returns the relative position of lookup_value within lookup_array. match_mode controls matching: 0 (exact, default), -1 (exact or next smaller), 1 (exact or next larger), 2 (wildcard). search_mode controls direction: 1 (first, default), -1 (last), 2/-2 (binary search for sorted data). It is the modern replacement for MATCH and accepts arrays directly.

howToSteps.name: Define the lookup
howToSteps.text: Choose the value to find and the array to search.

howToSteps.name: Pick match and search modes
howToSteps.text: Add match_mode and search_mode as needed.

howToSteps.name: Use the result
howToSteps.text: Feed the position into INDEX or other functions.

limitations: Microsoft 365 / Excel 2021+ only (also in newer Google Sheets).
Approximate modes (-1/1) require the array to be sorted correctly.

commonErrors.cause: Exact match (mode 0) found nothing, or spelling mismatch.
commonErrors.fix: Use mode -1/1 for approximate matches, or verify the lookup value.

commonErrors.cause: An invalid search_mode number was used.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: XMATCH is available in newer versions of Google Sheets with the same arguments and behavior as Excel.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Older Sheets lack XMATCH and would use MATCH instead.

faq.question: XMATCH vs MATCH?
faq.answer: XMATCH defaults to exact match, can search from the last, and supports wildcards and binary search; MATCH defaults to approximate.

faq.question: What is the default match mode?
faq.answer: Exact match (0), unlike MATCH's default approximate mode.

faq.question: Is XMATCH in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Yes, in newer Google Sheets versions; older Sheets only have MATCH.
